of the Battle; and a man in Sligo has told me that it will be so great a battle that
the horses shall go up to their fetlocks in blood, and that their girths, when it
is over, will rot from their bellies for lack of a hand to unbuckle them. If one
reads Rhys' Celtic Heathendom by the light of Frazer's Golden Bough, and puts
together what one finds there about the boar that killed Diarmuid, and other
old Celtic boars and sows, one sees that the battle is mythological, and that the
Pig it is named from must be a type of cold and winter doing battle with the
summer, or of death battling with life. 18 - I8gg-•go6.
